🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia’s return to war in Yemen could permanently shut Bab el-Mandeb, ignite Africa
Ansar Allah (the Houthis) has carried out a large-scale military operation targeting Saudi Aramco facilities in Abha, Najran, the Economic City, and Jizan, as well as [the King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74235)
The attack was in retaliation for 121 airstrikes across Marib, Al-Bayda, Hodeidah, Taiz, and Al-Jawf, launched by Saudi Arabia, according to Ansar Allah.
Meanwhile, Saudi proxy forces supported by the kingdom’s airpower have vowed to seize Sanaa.
👁 Saudi proxy advance on Al-Jawf and Al-Bayda
On September 7, fighting intensified in Taiz, Al-Jawf, and Al-Bayda, along key routes toward Houthi-held Sanaa. Ansar Allah said it repelled an offensive in Al-Jawf, inflicting significant casualties on pro-Saudi forces and [destroying military equipment.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74216)
Al-Jawf is strategically important because it borders Saudi Arabia and provides a potential corridor toward Saada, the Houthis’ main stronghold, according to Al Jazeera.
Al-Bayda is important for its central position in Yemen, linking eight governorates – four in the north and four in the south – and making it a key route for the movement of forces and supplies.
🪖 War is expanding: are Saudis engaging African mercs?
Earlier, unconfirmed reports claimed Saudi Arabia had deployed more than 30,000 troops from South Sudan, 10,000 from Somalia, and Syrian mercenaries into northern Yemen for a major, air-backed offensive on Sanaa.
If confirmed, the deployment would signal that Riyadh resumed its use of foreign ground forces in Yemen. Sudan previously contributed up to 30,000 troops to the Saudi-led coalition, according to a senior Sudanese military official in 2019, during the war that began in 2015 and largely subsided after[ the 2022 ceasefire.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72131)
Is Saudi Arabia up to a long-term conflict?
The US State Department has approved two weapons deals with Saudi Arabia worth $5.75 billion: $5 billion for 10,000 Boeing-made precision bomb kits and $750 million for Honeywell tank engines. The package also includes a comparable number of unguided bombs, making it one of the largest US-Saudi defense deals since the Iran war began.
The purchase indicates Riyadh is preparing to resume its war against the Houthis, with Saudi-backed mercenaries conducting ground operations inside Yemen while Saudi warplanes provide air support, the Weichert Report argues.
📊 Oil prices will only go up
Saudi Arabia’s previous war effort failed to defeat Ansar Allah and instead strengthened its resilience. Now, backed by defense pacts [with Turkey and Pakistan, ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73198)Riyadh believes it is better positioned to renew the war. Reports about Syrian mercenaries on the ground suggest Turkish involvement, while Donald Trump’s backing for Saudi Arabia’s July strike on Sanaa signals Washington’s support for further regional escalation.
But the consequences will extend far beyond Yemen. The Weichert Report predicts the escalation will close [the Bab el-Mandeb Strait](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72095), potentially permanently, and pull Africa deeper into the conflict. The resulting disruption to Red Sea shipping could choke Saudi oil exports, while renewed Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure could further destabilize global [oil markets.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74250)

Palestinian planners and architects are highlighting the hypocritical double standard: Jewish communities “expand” and “settle,” while Arab ones are framed as “invading.” 
In the Negev, Benjamin Netanyahu’s butcher, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, boasted of 5,700 demolitions in 2025.
